newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes steady, MidEast light premiums weaker.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes steady, MidEast light premiums weaker.

text.p: Asian crude prices held recent levels, but indications on light MidEast grades were showing a weaker market in March from February.
The market remained confused over a Qatar Marine deal, heard done at ADNOC plus 35 cents. Traders said they had expected the grade to achieve a higher premium nearer plus 50 cents.
But some traders said the Japanese seller was worried about expected volume of West African crude due into the region.
A major sold a Murban cargo into Kenya at ADNOC +52 cents, the first indication for Murban. The Murban market went out in February at ADNOC +80 cents.
The window for West African imports was being supported by an wide Brent/Tapis spread, but the spread was narrowing and on a March basis was valued around $1.42 per barrel.
In medium grades, traders heard a major sold one million barrels of Oman to China at MPM +26 cents, maintaining the premium for the last deal done.
March Masila was heard changing hands at dated Brent less 50 and 55 cents. The deals could not be confirmed.
Minas indications held firm and recent talk of two majors selling to China at premiums of $1.10 were dismissed as confusion over recent deals.

Talk of deals done higher than $1.20 was confirmed but only for cargoes that were date specific. One major said it had traded as high as $1.30 on dates and said talk of Minas done at $1.50 probably reflected similar arrangements.
In addition, a recent Duri deal at $1.10 was said to be date specific also.
Traders said they expected more market activity next week as refineries finally sort out their light and medium slates as they look towards the end of the first quarter.
